candidates.title: Centered 180° pizza turn using repeated short peel strokes
candidates.objective: With YAM holding a full-scale 7-inch turning peel, rotate a roughly 300 mm partially baked pizza about 180° inside a representative closed-roof 16-inch oven. Use repeated short, low-lift strokes so some pizza-to-stone contact remains at all times, keep the pizza within 50 mm of its initial center throughout, release it top-side-up on the stone, and withdraw the peel. Cooking chemistry and food safety are outside scope.
skills: full-scale long-handled tool grasp and steering
thin-blade insertion beneath a minimally compliant crust rim
repeated tangential traction with stroke resets
candidates.success_conditions: Using only the current native trial, award full credit when wrapped final yaw after release is 150–210°, maximum pizza-center excursion is no more than 50 mm at every recorded physics frame, pizza-to-deck contact remains present throughout, the pizza stays top-side-up and entirely inside the oven, no crust damage or topping loss occurs, and the peel is fully withdrawn. Award partial credit for 90–149° yaw only when all other full-credit conditions hold. Award zero for less than 90° yaw, excursion over 50 mm, any loss of deck contact, direct gripper contact with the pizza, taking the pizza outside the oven to turn it, overturning, crust penetration, permanent rim folding, topping separation, collision damage, pose writes, fake grasp welds, disabled collisions, or unreleased peel contact. Stroke count, hand identity, and action order are diagnostic only.
candidates.industrial_value: Represents the in-oven turning operation used in pizza preparation while testing long-tool control and manipulation of a weakly constrained food item in a confined, roofed workspace. The distinctive ability is tool-mediated under-edge insertion followed by centered rotation while deck support is continuously preserved, rather than generic rigid-object turning or pizza launching.
candidates.dexterity: High: the peel must enter beneath a compliant rim without puncturing it, apply several small tangential strokes without lifting the pizza clear of the deck, limit cumulative translation, release cleanly, and clear the oven mouth.

candidates.asset_plan: Create an independently authored representative fixture rather than claiming an exact product replica. Preserve the documented 630 × 580 × 370 mm oven exterior, 16-inch capacity, 15 mm cordierite deck, and 170 × 800 × 20 mm, 0.4 kg turning peel. Use a provisional 300 mm pizza with a set rigid underside/core and shallow rim compliance limited to what blade entry requires. Treat mouth height, interior roof profile, usable deck depth, peel-edge thickness, pizza mass, friction, restitution, and rim stiffness as disclosed modeling assumptions requiring calibration. Gate development in this order: real-YAM handle grasp; full-scale reach and mouth/roof clearance; low repeated insertion strokes with no food pose scripting; tangential traction with continuous deck contact; trajectory-wide center and wrapped-yaw measurement; release clearance; and complete withdrawal. Use normal YAM joint and gripper commands only.
candidates.risk: The 800 mm handle may exceed practical YAM reach or collide with the oven mouth; a thin peel can tunnel through the rim; uncalibrated friction or compliance can produce implausible traction, lift, or folding; and center error can accumulate across strokes. Any failed native-physics gate blocks the full demonstration—equipment may not be scaled down and hidden pivots, pose control, collision disabling, or relaxed scoring are prohibited.

candidates.title: Centered corrective 90° pizza turn
candidates.objective: Use the same full-scale turning peel and roofed oven to rotate a roughly 300 mm partially baked pizza approximately 90° using low, short strokes while retaining deck contact, limiting center excursion to 50 mm, releasing top-side-up inside the oven, and withdrawing the tool.
candidates.success_conditions: Full credit requires wrapped final yaw after release of 75–105°, maximum center excursion no more than 50 mm throughout the native trace, uninterrupted pizza-to-deck contact, top-side-up containment inside the oven, no crust damage or topping loss, and complete peel withdrawal. Partial credit requires 45–74° yaw with every other condition unchanged. Zero credit applies to direct gripper bypass, external rotation, support loss, overturning, penetration, damage, pose writes, welds, disabled collisions, or retained tool contact.
candidates.industrial_value: Represents a smaller corrective in-oven turn when one sector needs additional exposure, using the same real turning tool and confined contact mechanics.
candidates.dexterity: Emphasizes accurate initiation and stopping of tool-mediated yaw while suppressing translation and avoiding excess rim lift.

candidates.asset_plan: Reuse the documented full-scale oven, stone, peel, and representative pizza model from the half-turn objective. Validate stopping accuracy and complete physical release with native YAM actions before adopting the proposed angular band.
candidates.risk: The quarter-turn is shorter but its narrow stopping band may be dominated by uncalibrated peel-to-crust and crust-to-stone friction. No center pin, pivot, or hidden damping may be introduced.
missing_evidence: A native full-scale YAM trial has not established repeatable stopping within the proposed 75–105° band.
Contact parameters have not been calibrated against a representative partially baked crust.

candidates.title: Turn a pale crust sector toward the oven hot side
candidates.objective: From a varied initial yaw, identify a visibly pale rim sector and use the full-scale turning peel to bring it toward a defined hot-side direction while maintaining deck contact, no more than 50 mm center excursion, top-side-up containment, final release, and peel withdrawal.
candidates.success_conditions: Full credit requires the pale-sector centerline to finish within 20° of the hot-side marker after release, at least 60° wrapped yaw change, maximum center excursion no more than 50 mm throughout, continuous pizza-to-deck contact, top-side-up containment, no crust damage or topping loss, and full peel withdrawal. Partial credit permits 21–40° final angular error while retaining every other condition. Zero credit includes translation without required yaw, direct gripper bypass, external rotation, loss of deck contact, overturning, penetration, damage, pose writes, welds, disabled collisions, or retained peel contact.
candidates.industrial_value: Tests perception-guided correction of visibly uneven baking while preserving the real under-edge tool interaction and confined geometry.
candidates.dexterity: Adds direction, insertion-point, and stopping decisions to blade insertion, low-lift tangential traction, center control, release, and withdrawal.

candidates.asset_plan: Reuse the half-turn fixture and minimal compliant-rim model. Make browning asymmetry a read-only visual yaw marker with no collision or mass effect. Represent the hot side visually because heat transfer and cooking chemistry are excluded. Test every allowed initial yaw for native reach, insertion, traction, release, and withdrawal.
candidates.risk: The sources establish observation-guided turning but not a quantitative target-zone tolerance. Varied starting orientations may also require unreachable approaches in the roofed workspace.
missing_evidence: No acquired source establishes the proposed 20° hot-side tolerance.
Native full-scale reach and traction have not been demonstrated across the proposed initial-yaw range.

selection_reason: This is the only candidate that directly preserves the requested half-turn while making repeated short, low-lift strokes, continuous deck support, a 50 mm trajectory-wide center limit, wrapped post-release yaw, and withdrawal observable. Exact acquired-source excerpts ground the 630 × 580 × 370 mm oven envelope, 16-inch capacity, 15 mm stone, and 170 × 800 × 20 mm, 0.4 kg peel without concatenating separated source fields. The objective tests under-edge insertion, controlled tangential traction, cumulative center control, and confined release; it is distinct from the rejected miniature pizza-launch setup. The alternative objectives remain meaningful but require additional stopping-accuracy or varied-start evidence.
